correctness.rationale: Maximum ones in any circular window can be achieved starting at a 1-run boundary, so comparing prefixes P_U(n),P_C(n) of the two candidate rotations suffices. With a>=c the difference P_C-P_U increases up to n=a+b if b>d, then decreases; its positive maximum is min(c,b-d). If b<=d it is everywhere <=0. Thus a cycle has a periodically prefix-normal rotation iff (a-c)(b-d)<=0; equality cases and unique infinite word follow because the prefix-one counts determine a word. Necklace identification (a,b,c,d)~(c,d,a,b) gives the two rational generating series z^4/[(1-z)^2(1-z²)^2] and z^6/[(1-z)^2(1-z²)^2]. Direct independent circular windows checked all 625 quadruples 1<=a,b,c,d<=5. Infinite proof is case/series argument, not the finite test.
